architectQuote: There is a growing shift toward residences that feel more personal, more intentional, and more connected to their surroundings. Buyers are prioritizing design, scale, and privacy over sheer volume. OPUS responds to that shift.
description: OPUS Coconut Grove is a deliberately small, six-story building at 3137 SW 27th Avenue — 14 residences total: 12 three-bedroom homes across four residential floors, plus two four-bedroom penthouses on the top floors. Architecture by Miami's Kobi Karp with interiors by São Paulo studio João Armentano and landscape by David O. Inc., the building is positioned as an elevated alternative to the Grove's large-scale branded towers: no 200-unit HOA, no elevator banks, no sales gallery theatrics. Interiors feature premium porcelain flooring and countertops, European-designed cabinetry, Miele appliances, natural gas cooktops, and full-height laminated glass windows with ceiling heights up to 3.60 meters (nearly 12 feet). Each residence has a private terrace; residences 2B, 2D, and the penthouses include BBQ-ready infrastructure. Two to three assigned spaces per residence within a fully autonomous Klaus Multiparking system with EV charging capability, plus dedicated storage and individual wine cellars on the mezzanine. The rooftop carries a 4,300-square-foot sundeck with pool, outdoor gourmet kitchen and BBQ, fitness center, and spa with massage room, dry sauna, and steam room. The mezzanine level holds private offices, a conference room, children's playroom, wine cellars, and dedicated storage for each residence. Ground floor features a 24-hour reception and intimate lobby with 12-foot ceilings. Walking distance (under 5 minutes) to CocoWalk, the Grove's Michelin-starred restaurants, Monty's and the bayside yacht clubs, and top-rated schools.
editorialLine: Coconut Grove, at the scale of a house.
excerpt: 14 boutique residences by Kobi Karp and João Armentano in the heart of Coconut Grove. Broke ground April 2026. Rooftop pool and spa, Klaus automated parking, from ~$2.8M. 50%+ sold.

signals.title: Selling out ahead of the superstructure
signals.body: Unusually strong absorption for a Grove boutique project — the low-density format is finding its buyer without needing a sales-gallery spectacle, and remaining inventory will compress as vertical work progresses.

signals.title: Discount to delivered Grove product
signals.body: A meaningful discount to delivered branded Grove product in the same submarket, for a boutique offering — with under 18 months to delivery.

signals.title: $28M Arixa Capital construction loan
signals.body: Construction financing closed with Arixa Capital concurrent with April 2026 groundbreaking. Meta Development's first Miami project to enter vertical construction — Colette Residences in South Brickell follows. Lender due diligence on a small 14-unit boutique project signals conviction on the absorption story.

signals.title: 14 residences · constrained secondary supply
signals.body: One of the smallest new-construction programs in Coconut Grove. At full absorption, secondary supply will be structurally constrained — unlike 100+ unit towers where resale competition is built into the asset. Half the inventory is already off-market.

signals.title: Kobi Karp, João Armentano, David O.
signals.body: Kobi Karp is among Miami's most prolific luxury architects. João Armentano brings a São Paulo residential voice rarely seen here. David O. landscape ties the team together. Klaus automated parking with EV charging is uncommon at 14 units.

signals.title: < 5 minutes to Grove village core
signals.body: 3137 SW 27th Avenue sits in the walkable South Grove corridor — under 5 minutes on foot to CocoWalk, Michelin-starred restaurants, marinas, and Grove retail. Distinct from Grove Isle / Fair Isle waterfront product. The play here is village walkability, not bayfront exposure.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: OPUS counter-positions against the Grove's large-scale pipeline (Four Seasons Coconut Grove, Vita at Grove Isle, The Fairchild). For buyers who have rejected the 200-unit tower experience but still want new construction, full amenities, and Coconut Grove walkability, the submarket has almost no direct comp. Strong pre-sales velocity and a closed construction loan validate the thesis — the market is selecting for low-density, design-led product.
investmentIntelligence.footnote: HOA: Est. $2.04/sq ft/month · Delivery: Estimated 2027 · Groundbreaking: April 2026 · Buyer representation: Zachary Akers, ONE Sotheby's International Realty (direct developer channel)
